question:
Fill in the blank.

In an age of instant messages and constant notifications, the ability to read deeply has become increasingly rare. Deep reading does not merely mean moving one’s eyes over printed words; it requires attention, patience and the willingness to follow an argument from its beginning to its conclusion. A reader who is always (1)____ by digital alerts may gather information quickly, but he seldom understands it fully. Schools, therefore, must not treat reading as a mechanical exercise. They should encourage students to question ideas, connect them with experience and reflect (2)____ what they have read. Such habits help learners develop judgement rather than simply collect facts. When reading is practised regularly, it also improves writing, because the mind absorbs patterns of clear expression. Many students avoid difficult texts because they appear demanding at first, yet these texts often give (3)____ to the most valuable insights. The challenge is not to make every passage easy, but to teach students how to stay with complexity without giving up. A society that values serious reading is likely to produce citizens who are less (4)____ to rumours and more capable of independent thought. Thus, reading is not a luxury; it is a discipline that strengthens both language and reason. Its importance will remain (5)____, even as technology changes the ways in which people receive information.
